content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The bookmark manager specification is ready for review.

- [Specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `specs/001-bookmark-manager`
- Validation: all 16 quality checks passed; no unresolved clarifications

The draft defines saving, searching, tags, editing, archiving, and confirmed deletion. It assumes a private, single-user, single-device first release; accounts, sharing, sync, import/export, and browser extensions are excluded.

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. I’ll only proceed to the implementation plan after approval.

Thanks — I read through it, and it's a clear write-up. A lot of it matches what I pictured: saving links, searching, tags, editing, archiving versus deleting with a confirmation. But going through it carefully, there are some things I really want that either aren't here or were set aside, and a couple I'd want changed before I'd feel good approving.

The biggest one: I don't want to type in the title myself. When I paste a link, I'd expect the app to go grab the page's title and description for me automatically — ideally the little site icon and a preview image too — and then let me tweak that text if I want. Making the title a required thing I have to fill in by hand is not what I had in mind. I saw that automatic fetching is listed as "outside scope," and that's the part I'd push back on hardest — for me that's core to what makes this worth using.

A few more that matter to me:

- **Read later.** I want to be able to mark a link as "to read," and then have a way to look at just my unread ones, and mark them read when I'm done. That whole idea seems to be missing.
- **Smarter searching.** Beyond plain text, I'd want to search by tag directly (something like typing the tag with a `#`), search an exact phrase, and combine things like "this AND that, but NOT the other." Just matching text isn't quite enough for me once I have a lot saved.
- **Handling several at once.** When I'm tidying up, I'd like to select a bunch of bookmarks and, say, tag them or archive them all together, instead of one at a time.
- **Sorting.** I'd want to choose the order sometimes — by title, by date — not only newest-first.
- **Notes with formatting.** When I write a note on a bookmark, I'd like to be able to format it a bit and have it show up nicely.

There are a few other things I had in the back of my mind — keeping a saved copy of a page so I don't lose it if the site disappears, saving a search I use often so I can come back to it, and bringing in / taking out my existing browser bookmarks — but I understand if some of those come later. The ones above, especially the automatic title-and-preview fetching and the read-later idea, are the ones I'd want reflected before we move on.

Can you revise the spec with those in mind?

content:
The specification has been revised and revalidated.

Major additions:

- Automatic title, description, site icon, and preview-image retrieval
- Address-derived fallback title when metadata is unavailable
- Editable retrieved details
- Read-later, unread, and read states
- `#tag`, quoted phrase, Boolean, and grouped searches
- Title and saved-date sorting
- Multi-select and bulk organization
- Formatted notes with basic rich-text options
- Explicitly deferred offline copies, saved searches, and browser import/export

All 16 quality checks pass with no unresolved clarifications.

- [Revised specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)

Please approve this revision or identify any further changes. I’ll wait for approval before producing the implementation plan.

This is a big improvement — it really captures what I was after. The automatic page details with a sensible fallback title, the read-later flow, the smarter searching, sorting, selecting several at once, and the formatted notes are all there the way I imagined. And I'm fine with saving offline copies, reusable searches, and browser import/export coming in a later round.

Two smaller things about tags I want to make sure are covered, since I'll be leaning on tags a lot:

- When I'm typing a tag onto a bookmark, I'd like it to suggest tags I've already used so I pick the existing one instead of accidentally creating a slightly different duplicate.
- And when I see a tag on a bookmark in the list, I'd like to be able to click it and have the library narrow down to just that tag, without typing a search.

I saw searching by tag and filtering by tag mentioned, so the second one may already be the intent — I just want it to be an easy click, not only something I type. Could you fold those two in? Once those are reflected, I'm happy with the specification and you can move on to the plan.

content:
The tag refinements are now explicit in the approved [specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md):

- Existing tags are suggested while typing, with prefix matches prioritized.
- Suggestions support keyboard and pointer selection.
- Clicking a displayed tag immediately applies it as an exact filter.
- These behaviors are covered by acceptance scenarios, requirements FR-026/FR-027, and success criterion SC-010.

The implementation plan is ready for review:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md)
- [Technical research](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/data-model.md)
- [HTTP API contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [Search grammar](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/search-grammar.md)
- [Validation quickstart](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/quickstart.md)

The design uses Node.js 24 LTS, React/Fastify, SQLite FTS5, guarded metadata retrieval, locally cached preview assets, and structured rich-text notes. These choices align with the current [Node release schedule](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases), [SQLite FTS5 guidance](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html), and [OWASP SSRF guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html).

The OpenAPI contract validates successfully; its only advisory warnings concern the undecided project license and the health endpoint lacking an artificial 4xx response. No application code has been written.

Please approve the plan or request changes. Task generation and implementation remain gated on that approval.

Honestly, most of the technical detail here is beyond me — the choice of tools and how it's wired together I'll trust you on. What matters to me is that the plan is built to deliver everything we settled on: the automatic titles and previews with a fallback, the read-later flow, the tag suggestions and click-to-filter, the smarter searching, sorting, selecting several at once, formatted notes, and the archive-versus-delete safety with confirmation.

If the plan covers all of that and you're confident in it, then yes — go ahead and move on to the next step. I'll do my real judging when I can see it working.

content:
The bookmark manager is ready to try at:

**http://maker:4000/**

It includes automatic page details with fallbacks, read-later, advanced search and sorting, tag suggestions and click-to-filter, formatted notes, bulk actions, and safe archive/delete flows.

I left the library empty so you can test the complete saving experience yourself. All 69 automated checks pass, including browser, accessibility, security, and 10,000-bookmark performance tests. The dependency audit reports zero vulnerabilities.

I spent a while actually putting it through its paces, and it does what we agreed on. Saving a link gives me a sensible title even when a page has nothing to offer, and when I tried to save the same address twice it stopped me and pointed me back to the one I already had. The read-later side works — I could mark things unread and see just those. Searching is genuinely the part I was most worried about, and it held up: pulling up a tag with `#`, an exact phrase in quotes, and mixing things like "travel but not the book one" or "rome and either article or book" all returned exactly what I expected, regardless of capitalization. Typing part of a tag suggested one I'd already used, and narrowing to a single tag worked as a simple filter. Sorting, selecting several and acting on them together, and the archive-then-delete safety all behaved — it wouldn't let me permanently delete anything that wasn't archived, and it insisted on a clear confirmation first.

This is what I wanted for a first version. The few things we set aside earlier — keeping an offline copy of a page, saving a search I reuse a lot, and bringing bookmarks in and out from a browser — I do still want eventually, so please keep those on the list for a later round. But none of them hold up what you've built here.

I'm happy with it. Nicely done.
